claims.finding: LexinFintech suspended its share repurchase programme at the Q1 2026 call - after buying 441k shares at $6.37 in late Aug 2025, 1.79m at $5.87 in September and 1.28m at $4.31 in October per the buyback table on p.174 of the FY2025 20-F - and the long thesis visible across the capture is almost entirely a bet that a new, larger buyback plus a maintained dividend lands with this print ('this will fucking fly like crazy when the new buyback is announced', 'Monday with the new buyback I wouldn't be surprised LX flying 50%').
claims.why_not_priced: The capture shows the option flow with calls leading puts 10:9 into the event and a retail base that has explicitly sized positions on a capital-return announcement, i.e. the price contains a call option on a corporate action that the company's own last call removed. A market pricing 'no buyback, dividend cut' would not have calls over puts and would not have bid the ADR up 2.2% on 2026-08-28 on the heaviest volume of the run-in (4.86m vs a 1.98m 20-day average). The buyback-suspension fact is not in any wire item in this capture - it reaches the corpus only as a shareholder recollection of the Q1 call, and the purchase prices come from page 174 of a 20-F that nobody aggregates.
claims.independence: Same-direction, different corpus file: filings.json shows a Form 4 accepted 2026-08-21T12:27:05Z, ten days before the print and at the all-time low, preceded by 144 notices of intent to sell on 2025-09-19 and 2025-11-26 - https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1708259/000119312526360007/xslF345X06/ownership.xml (direction of the Form 4 transaction is not recoverable from the index, so this is corroboration of insider activity only, not of its sign).

claims.finding: Every relevant peer reported in the ten days before LX and the corpus records the reaction function: FinVolution printed a beat on 2026-08-27 and reiterated full-year 2026 revenue guidance of RMB 11.5-12.9bn and still fell more than 15%, while Qifu's call 'read like the fall of an empire' - and the reason is on the record, that China lending volumes fell roughly 40-50% in August after the Juzi platform incident, with banks cutting lending lines and short-term risk rates up 20%, all of which falls in Q3 and none of which is in the June quarter LX is about to report.
claims.corpus_ref: docs/577e46b84b8aa280f5960f5306d50aa466c89561.txt, messages of 2026-08-28T03:42:02Z (FINV call summary, August volumes -40-50%), 2026-08-28T00:35:04Z, 2026-08-29T07:53:00Z, 2026-08-26T15:50:48Z ('the Q2 figures next week should be similar to Q1 since none of the damage occurred until after the quarter was done')
claims.why_not_priced: The corpus shows holders drawing the opposite inference from the same events - FINV's beat is being read as bullish for LX ('$LX flying after hours 7% as a reaction... Major squeeze coming Monday') - when the actual FINV tape says a good print plus reiterated guidance was worth minus fifteen percent in this sector this week. The information content of Monday's release is therefore entirely in the Q3 outlook, and LX is described in its own shareholder base as the operator with 'the needed scale to survive, but just barely'. If the market had priced guidance rather than the quarter, the ADR would not have closed higher on 08-28 on record volume.
claims.independence: WARNING - shares a source with finding 1: both rest on docs/577e46b84b8aa280f5960f5306d50aa466c89561.txt, the single 90-message stocktwits aggregate that is the only substantive body in this capture. The independent corroboration for this one is the run-in in quote.json: -19.2% over 20 days to an all-time low of 1.155 on 08-27 on rising volume, which is the sector shock arriving in the price without any LX-specific disclosure in filings.json since the Q1 6-K of 2026-05-26.
